fields.v: One internal repository, 7 future test tasks, 24 learning commits. Configurations: skill-conditioned agent vs baseline agent without skills, under 4 conditions (sequential/parallel x by-category/all). Baseline: same agent and tools without skill document. Held constant: model (Claude Opus 4.6), tool-use capabilities, tasks. Acceptance: oracle diffs (no tests). Repetitions: not stated (apparently one run per condition). Human intervention: none stated

Skills better in 3 of 4 conditions on File IoU: +19 pts in seq-all (80% vs 61%), +12 in par-bycat, +9 in par-all, tie in seq-bycat (71%); seq-all 21% fewer steps (56.8 vs 71.9), other settings within 1.4 steps; line deviation lower in 3 of 4 (higher in seq-bycat, 1.22 vs 1.13). Overall win rate >50%: Gemini judge 3 of 4 settings (57%, 58%, 54%; seq-bycat 46%), Claude judge 2 of 4 (54%, 55%; par-all 46%, seq-bycat 26%), although the text says 3 of 4 under both judges. par-bycat by dimension: skill ahead on Q2 logic (50% vs 25%) and Q3 redundancy (54% vs 41%), baseline ahead on Q1 scope (41% vs 25%) and Q4 style (38% vs 27%). No significance test

rev.why: Draft said File IoU +8 to +12 in par conditions (Table 2 gives +12 and +9) and 'win rates >50% in 3 of 4 settings per judge', but Table 3 shows only 2 of 4 under the Claude judge.

fields.v: Partly distinguished conditions (seq-bycat no gain). Repeatability not assessed (7 tasks; baseline values differ between conditions although the baseline has no skills, not explained). Limitations stated: LLM-judge bias, single internal repository

Validated on one internal repository only; generalisation to open-source GitHub repositories needed; LLM judges may be biased or inaccurate, more verifiable metrics needed; transfer of skills to broader tasks and established benchmarks open; skills help localisation and reuse but not surface style; skills can induce over-caution (redundant guard)

Table 4 (p. 7) jumbled by pdftotext; rebuilt from row sums and text p. 6: Q1 skill 25 / base 41 / tie 34; Q2 50/25/25; Q3 54/41/5; Q4 27/38/36. Inconsistencies: abstract and conclusion claim functional correctness and "significantly improve" but no tests or statistics; text p. 6 says the skill agent wins in 3 of 4 settings under both judges, but Table 3 shows 2 of 4 >50% under the Claude judge (par-all 46%, seq-bycat 26%); text p. 7 gives File IoU gains of +10–18% while Table 2 gives +19, +12, +9 and 0 pts; contribution says the benchmark is released, but the repository is internal and no link is given; baseline values differ across the four settings although the baseline has no skills; inter-judge agreement rates promised but not reported numerically; 386 of 2,738 commits is called 'a 77.2% suitability rate' (p. 6), but 386/2,738 = 14.1%. Values used: Tables 2-4. No replication package. No pre-registration. Language not stated

rev.why: Two reporting inconsistencies were missing: the 'both judges' claim vs Table 3, and the '+10–18%' File IoU claim vs Table 2.
A further reporting inconsistency was missing: the 77.2% suitability rate on p. 6 does not match 386/2,738 (14.1%).
